title: Why some couples are comfortable with silence, according to psychology
description: Silence in romantic relationships can signal comfort or discomfort based on personal communication styles and emotional needs. The 2024 study revealed that chosen silence often indicates emotional security and closeness. Alternatively, silence resulting from anxiety or hostility may lead to misunderstandings and emotional distance. Understanding each other's preferences regarding conversation and quiet time can strengthen relationships. Ultimately, intimacy is shaped by both meaningful conversations and moments of peaceful silence.

Although the Shamonda virus has been prevalent in livestock, no general health risk has currently been identified.

title: Why some people struggle to say no even when exhausted, according to psychology
description: Saying yes to others' requests can be a common pattern for people-pleasers, leading to stress and overcommitment. This habit stems from a fear of disappointing others, which can make saying no feel uncomfortable. Continued agreement may cause emotional exhaustion and hinder personal relationships. Effective strategies for setting boundaries include pausing before answering requests and practicing refusal in low-pressure situations.

Consequently, the court rejected the bank's request for a summary judgment against the estate of Alice McNamara.

title: Security concerns: Delhi Police denies permission for Diljit Dosanjh's Oct 30 concert

Fans are left disappointed as the festive season approaches, with security concerns and law and order issues influencing this decision. Organizers are now faced with the challenge of possibly seeking new permits or rescheduling the concert, marking a setback for the Aura India Tour.

title: Florida girl named in sperm donor's will loses claim to his house
description: A Florida appeals court has upheld the rejection of a young girl's claim to a deceased man's house, despite his having named her in his will. The dispute involved a 2017 sperm donor agreement between Melissa Azrack and Malcolm Dorman. The appeal failed because Azrack did not challenge the lower court's finding that the property was not protected homestead property.

title: Meta Q3 results: Net income jumps 264% to $9.86 bn, but legal charge limit profits
description: Meta Platforms reported a net income of $9.86 billion in Q3 2026, tripling from the previous year. Overall revenue increased to $64.60 billion, primarily driven by higher advertising earnings. However, operating income declined due to a significant legal charge linked to teen mental health litigation. The company plans to invest heavily in artificial intelligence infrastructure to support future revenue growth.

US soldier killed at 17 in Korean War identified after 75 years, to be buried
description: Pvt. Joseph E. Boyd, who went missing in action at just 17 during the Korean War, has finally been identified decades later. His remains, previously known as Unknown X-1642, have been matched to his identity through advanced forensic techniques, including DNA testing. A dignified burial ceremony is set for October 21, 2026, in Owings Mills, Maryland, underscoring the ongoing commitment to honor missing service members from historical conflicts.

title: Facial laser session leaves woman with burns; consumer panel orders Rs 1.11 lakh payout
description: In an alarming incident at Berkowits Hair & Skin Clinic in Bengaluru, a woman suffered severe second-degree burns during a laser hair removal treatment. Despite her intense pain, the technician minimized her discomfort, labeling it as normal. Subsequent medical examinations validated her injuries. The district consumer commission held the clinic accountable for inadequate service and mandated compensation, including a refund and damages for her injuries and emotional distress.

title: 'Am studying his body': Trump goes into graphic detail about US senator's body at rally
Virginia teen's model improves simulated earthquake sensor coverage by 16.7%
description: A 14-year-old student from Williamsburg, Virginia, has become one of 30 finalists in a national science competition after developing a mathematical model to improve earthquake sensor placement. Isabel Rossi's six-month research project showed that adding just five sensors could increase simulated detection coverage by 16.7%. She used earthquake records from California and mathematical methods to identify better sensor locations.

title: 'Beacon of hope': Polish PM Tusk hails ties with India, calls PM Modi a 'friend'
description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk visited India to strengthen bilateral cooperation between India and Poland. He highlighted the absence of conflicts of interest and shared values between the two nations. Both leaders discussed expanding economic opportunities through the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement. Tusk emphasized the positive economic developments achieved by Poland and India over the last 35 years.

description: Raihan Vadra's photography exhibition, No Idea Is Fine, allegedly faced turmoil at Bikaner House when management objected hours before its start, claiming venue policy violations. While Vadra proposed removing select images, the officials demanded the removal of all 70 photographs, including those depicting the Indian national flag. This sparked outrage among Congress members, igniting debates about censorship and the value of artistic freedom.

title: Texas man, 86, spends 39 years building 62-foot boat; strangers step in
description: An 86-year-old man from Mineral Wells, Texas, has been building a 62-foot steel boat since 1987. After three visitors discovered his ambition, they launched a crowdfunding campaign to support the project. More than $41,000 has been raised towards completing the boat and moving it to a launch site. The remaining work on the vessel is expected to require about $50,000 in funding.

title: Viral fever, vomiting: How Praveen Kumar fought back to win Asian Para Games gold
description: Praveen Kumar won the men’s high jump T44/64 gold medal at the Asian Para Games in Japan. He accomplished this while dealing with a hip injury and battling fever, cold, and cough. Despite these challenges, he cleared 2.05m, setting a new Games record. His previous record was 1.95m in the T44 category. Praveen aims to defend his Paralympic title at the next Los Angeles Games.

title: Ebay to cut 1,000 jobs; CEO says ‘Our strategy is working’ amid luxury push
description: EBay plans to eliminate approximately 9% of its workforce to simplify operations and promote growth. The company focuses on authenticated luxury items and collectables in response to market demand. Following earlier layoffs in February, EBay aims to shift resources to faster-growing sectors. EBay has recently made strategic acquisitions, including the fashion platform Depop, boosting its resale market position. The company anticipates higher third-quarter revenue, exceeding Wall Street expectations.

title: After renaming Lake Ontario, Google CEO rejects US request to rename Atlantic Ocean
description: President Trump has recently proposed renaming the Atlantic Ocean, following prior discussions about the Atlantic Ocean. During a recent event, he mentioned contacting Google Maps regarding these renaming efforts. Google CEO Sundar Pichai reportedly declined his proposal on the grounds that oceans encompass multiple countries. This follows the US administration's earlier renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users.

title: Paid Rs 1 lakh for gold chain, got nothing; jeweller ordered to pay Rs 1.3 lakh
description: Himachal Pradesh state consumer commission upheld a decision directing Shri Ganesh Jewellers to refund Rs 1 lakh. Customer M R Chauhan made an advance payment for a gold chain that was never delivered. Despite repeated requests and a police complaint, the jeweller failed to return the money. The commission awarded compensation of Rs 20,000 for mental harassment and Rs 10,000 for litigation costs.
